questions.question: Walk me through the kitchen remodel so far.
questions.expected_answer: Sept 8: Argus asked Rick Alvarez (Alvarez Kitchen & Bath) for a quote. Sept 15: Rick's site visit; he measured, and Mara wants the sink moved to an island. Sept 21: Birchwood Remodeling (Hannah Lee) estimated $44,900 including the island sink, about eight weeks, starting in January. Sept 23: Rick quoted $38,400 with the sink staying put (about $4,500 more to move it), five to six weeks, starting the week of Nov 16. Sept 24: they leaned toward Rick. Sept 28: Argus asked Rick for a revised quote with the island sink and a butcher-block island top. Sept 29: Rick promised it by Friday Oct 2. It never came; Argus followed up Oct 8 with no reply. As of Oct 13 they're leaning toward Birchwood.

questions.question: What's happened with my blood work?
questions.expected_answer: Dr. Ortiz ordered fasting blood work at the Sept 16 physical, and Argus booked the draw for Thursday Oct 8 at 7:30 am. On Oct 2 the clinic moved it to Tuesday Oct 13 at 7:30 am because the lab was closing Oct 8 for an equipment upgrade. Argus did the draw on Oct 13; results are due in the patient portal in 3 to 5 days and haven't come in yet.

questions.question: Which swim lesson time does Mara want for the kids?

She first preferred the Tuesday/Thursday 5:30 pm class (Sept 15), when her late shifts were Mon/Wed/Fri, but switched to Saturdays (Oct 5) because her late shifts move to Tuesday and Thursday from the week of Oct 19.

questions.question: Which contractor are we leaning toward for the kitchen?
questions.expected_answer: Birchwood Remodeling (Hannah Lee), as of Oct 13, even though it costs more ($44,900), because Rick never sent the revised quote he promised by Oct 2 and didn't answer the Oct 8 follow-up. On Sept 24 they had been leaning toward Rick ($38,400, about $42,900 with the island sink, and an earlier start).

questions.question: What have I said I'd do that I still haven't done?

Call North Star Sports Medicine to book the knee appointment (said he would the week of Sept 16; still hadn't by Sept 26). questions.question: Walk me through the basement flood and the insurance claim.
questions.expected_answer: Overnight April 18-19 a storm flooded the finished basement with about two inches of water because the old sump pump never turned on; Sean Brennan brought dehumidifiers and recommended DryRight Restoration. April 20: Argus filed a claim with Great Plains Mutual (GP-26-118734); the plumber found the pump's float switch stuck, and DryRight began the dry-out (done April 24, when the plumber also put in a new pump with battery backup for $1,280, which insurance didn't cover). April 28: the adjuster, Denise Hart, inspected with Mara. May 5: her estimate, under the water backup endorsement ($10,000 limit, $1,000 deductible): $3,400 to DryRight directly and $5,600 to Argus and Mara. Birchwood Remodeling (Hannah Lee) quoted $9,800 with vinyl plank flooring and rebuilt the basement from June 22; mold found behind the utility room wall added $2,300 and pushed the finish to July 10 ($12,100 in all). Great Plains approved a $2,300 mold supplement on July 21 and closed the claim on August 4, having paid $11,300. Out of pocket: about $5,480 ($4,200 to Birchwood beyond insurance, plus the $1,280 pump).

questions.question: How did the cabin week come together, and where do things stand now?
questions.expected_answer: April 26: Kate Brennan proposed that the Brennans, the Okafors, and the McNevanses share a lake cabin in August; everyone was in, and they settled on August 9-15. May 6-8: Kate found and booked Loon Song Cabin on Lake Namakagon through LakeStays on her card, $2,850, or $950 per family. In June she split up the dinners (the McNevanses cooked Monday and Thursday, and Argus brought the cooler and camp stove), and on July 30 she passed on the owner's rules, including no fireworks. The trip was August 9-15 (Theo caught his first walleye). August 16: Kate asked each family for $950 by September 1. Argus paid on August 17. Okie (Ben Okafor) said he'd pay by September 1, didn't, said on September 22 he'd pay "this weekend", and as of October 8 still hadn't.

questions.question: What's happened with the van this year?
questions.expected_answer: April 23: a recall notice for the 2016 Odyssey's sliding door latch. May 14: Lakes Honda did the recall repair and an oil change (128,400 miles) and warned that the transmission shudders and will likely need a $4,000-5,000 replacement. July 20: after a bad shudder on the freeway, Argus and Mara decided to replace it before winter. August 6-7: they test-drove and put a $500 deposit on a used 2022 Toyota Sienna XLE at Northland Toyota ($36,500, from Megan Doyle), for pickup September 17. They offered the Odyssey to Jerome Wells on August 24 for $9,500; he test-drove it and offered $9,000, which they accepted. They picked up the Sienna on September 17, and Jerome picked up the Odyssey on September 19 with a $9,000 cashier's check.

questions.question: Who said we couldn't have fireworks at the cabin?
questions.expected_answer: The cabin's owner, Linda Marsh, secondhand: she told Kate Brennan on the phone, and Kate passed it on in her July 30 email about the cabin rules (no fireworks because of the fire danger and because the neighbors complain). Argus never heard from Linda directly.

questions.question: Whose idea was the vinyl plank floor in the basement?
questions.expected_answer: Hannah Lee's, of Birchwood Remodeling: her May 19 estimate suggested luxury vinyl plank instead of carpet because it survives another flood and carpet doesn't. Mara then wanted it (May 20), and Argus accepted the estimate with it on May 21.

questions.question: Has everyone paid Kate back for the cabin?
questions.expected_answer: No. Argus paid the McNevanses' $950 on August 17, but Okie (Ben Okafor) still owes the Okafors' $950. He promised it by September 1, missed that, told Kate on September 22 he'd send it "this weekend", and as of October 8 Kate said he still hadn't paid. It's overdue.

questions.question: Is there anyone who asked me for something and never heard back?
questions.expected_answer: Sean Brennan. On September 14 he asked whether Argus still had the two dehumidifiers he lent the night of the April flood, and asked for them back that week; nothing shows Argus replied or returned them (as of June 1 they were still in the garage). The suspicious emails asking for money or passwords don't count, and Ben's Austin request got a reply.

questions.question: Did the insurance adjuster ever get the plumber's invoice she asked for?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, but from Mara, not Argus. Denise Hart (Great Plains Mutual) asked for it on April 22, and Argus said he'd send it once he had it. The plumber left the paper invoice with Mara, and Mara emailed Denise a photo of it on April 27 while Argus was in Denver; Denise confirmed that afternoon that she had it.

questions.question: Which email addresses does Okie write to me from?
questions.expected_answer: Okie is Ben Okafor. Two addresses: his personal ben.okafor@example.com (for example the Austin trip email on September 17 and his September 22 reply about the cabin money) and ben@okafor-studio.example, his new design studio's address, which he has used since April 28 (the cabin planning, the fishing invite, the website favor).

questions.question: What did the plumber say was wrong with our sump pump?
questions.expected_answer: That it was the original pump from when the house was built, about 15 years old, and its float switch had stuck, so it never turned on during the April storm. He came April 20, replaced it on April 24 with a new pump plus a battery backup ($1,280), and his invoice says the old pump failed because the float switch stuck. Nothing captured gives his name.

questions.question: How do I know Hannah Lee?
questions.expected_answer: She's with Birchwood Remodeling. A coworker of Mara's recommended Birchwood after the April flood, and Hannah rebuilt the basement (estimate May 19, work June 22 to July 10, including the mold change order, $12,100). In September she quoted the kitchen remodel ($44,900 with the island sink), and as of October 13 Argus and Mara are leaning toward Birchwood for the kitchen.

questions.question: Who outside our family was part of both the basement flood and the cabin trip?
questions.expected_answer: Sean Brennan, Kate's husband (Olivia's dad). The morning after the April flood he brought two dehumidifiers and a wet-vac and recommended DryRight Restoration, and in September he asked for the dehumidifiers back. He and Kate and their kids shared the cabin on Lake Namakagon in August.

questions.question: Who bought our old van, and how do we know them?
questions.expected_answer: Jerome Wells, Tasha Okafor's brother (Tasha is Okie's wife). Okie mentioned at the cabin on August 14 that Jerome needed a used minivan; Argus offered him the Odyssey on August 24, they agreed on $9,000, and Jerome picked it up on September 19 with a cashier's check.

questions.question: What paint color did we use on the basement walls?
questions.expected_answer: Sherwin-Williams Agreeable Gray (SW 7029), in eggshell. Argus told the assistant on July 14, and said there's a leftover gallon under the basement stairs. It isn't anywhere else.

questions.question: What's the confirmation number for the cabin rental?
questions.expected_answer: Unknown. Kate booked Loon Song Cabin on her own LakeStays account, and her emails give the dates, check-in and check-out times, the address, and the door code, but no confirmation number. The LakeStays emails in Argus's inbox are only marketing.
